title: Building interiors keep the exterior window glow instead of DFU's WindowStyle.Disabled (black)
claim: DFU lays out interior models with SetClimate(..., WindowStyle.Disabled) (DaggerfallInterior.cs:473/:517/:1270); Disabled sets EmissionColor black (MaterialReader.cs:934-936). Port: interiorContext.js:120 uploads window masks via uploadRecord (dataPipeline.js:89-91); drawMesh binds them (renderer.js:1578) times the global _windowEmission (renderer.js:1114-1115), which is only ever day/night/fog: main.js:67 boots it 'day'; world.js:3295 / exterior.js:1607 write it only in exterior frames (world.js:3070 modal return exits first); worldModes' interior block (:2779-2796) never calls setWindowEmission; WINDOW_STYLES (windowEmission.js:8-13) has no disabled entry.
consequence: Inside every shop/tavern/house, window glass glows pale blue by day and amber at night where DFU/classic show unlit glass; contradicts the port's own bible (Rendering-Arc R2 note: 'emission stays dark (Disabled)').

title: Dispatcher's Day window style overrides the ?interior scene's documented dark emission
claim: main.js:67 runs renderer.setWindowEmission(windowEmissionRGB(params.get('window') || 'day')) BEFORE routing (the ?interior route is line 68), overwriting the renderer's black boot value (renderer.js:468). interior.js:28-30 documents the DFU law it relies on - 'SetClimate with WindowStyle.Disabled - emission stays dark here by default' - and neither interior.js nor interiorContext.js ever calls setWindowEmission, so 'by default' meant the renderer's boot state, which the dispatcher line defeats. The standalone-scene slice of the previous finding: the port disagrees with its own comment one import away.
consequence: The standalone ?interior dev scene draws climate-swapped window records with a day-blue glow instead of the dark glass the scene header and DFU (MaterialReader.cs:934-936) both specify.

title: Four BEAST_DESIGNS entries quote wrong ENEMY_BASICS level/damage
claim: The design-line convention (orcBody.js:12 'anchored to ENEMY_BASICS, not invented'; test/atronachs.test.js:20 pins its numbers) quotes each enemy's EnemyBasics level/damage, but four beasts.js entries diverge from EnemyBasics.cs: GrizzlyBear port 8/[1,20] (beasts.js:127-128) vs C# Level 4, 1-8 (cs:380-388); SabertoothTiger 10/[1,25] (:149-150) vs 4, 1-10 (:413-421); Spider 3/[1,8] (:216-217) vs 4, 5-15 (:446-450); GiantScorpion 9/[1,20] (:237-238) vs 12, 15-25 (:912-916). The port's combat table characters/enemyBasics.js is correct for all four ids (verified), so only these labels are wrong; BEAST_DESIGNS feeds only paperdollPayload.js beastPacks.
consequence: The voxel editor's stat readout shows wrong level/damage for these four enemies; combat is unaffected because ENEMY_BASICS is correct.

title: resolvePaperdollRecord/isCloak have no src caller; law duplicated inline
claim: resolvePaperdollRecord (paperdollArt.js:20-27) and its exported isCloak helper - the file's stated verbatim port of DaggerfallUnityItem.GetInventoryTextureRecord's variant resolution (cs:1740-1764) - have no caller in src/ (grep finds only test/paperdollart.test.js and test/piece.test.js); the live copy of the same record law is re-implemented inline in systems/itemTemplates.js:133-144 with its own private CLOAK_TEMPLATES set (itemTemplates.js:79), so two copies exist and only the inline one runs.
consequence: No player-visible effect today (copies agree), but a fix applied to the exported 'one home' copy - e.g. the C# IsArtifact carve-out at DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:1746-1748, absent from both - would never reach the running path.

title: Wraith design damage [10,45] contradicts EnemyBasics MinDamage 20
claim: undeadBody.js:467 gives the Wraith design 'damage: [10, 45]' in a file whose sibling entries cite ENEMY_BASICS as source (e.g. Zombie :112). DFU EnemyBasics.cs:1016-1017 has Wraith MinDamage = 20, MaxDamage = 45, and the port's own combat table src/characters/enemyBasics.js ('23', lines 1024-1025) correctly carries minDamage 20 / maxDamage 45. title: canAccessLibrary ported but library bookshelves are absent entirely
claim: DFU gates guild library bookshelves on guild.CanAccessLibrary() (DaggerfallBookshelf.cs:74; Temple.cs:466, MagesGuild.cs:129 rank>=2). The port translated the gate faithfully (guildServices.js:286-290, zero callers) but the consumer never got built: worldModes.js:638 returns for any non-shop building with the comment 'Library/Guild/Temple bookshelves ... pend (FLAGGED)'.
consequence: Mages Guild and temple libraries are unreadable at any rank - the rank-2 library privilege the port already computes buys nothing.

title: Make Potions opens with zero ingredients instead of the record-34 refusal
claim: DFU MakePotionService scans pack+wagon for any ingredient and pops MessageBox(NoPotionIngredients) when none exist (GuildServicePopupWindow.cs:670-686). The port ports the id (NO_POTION_INGREDIENTS=34, guildServiceFlow.js:31, zero callers) but worldModes.js:1736-1758 opens the PotionMakerWindow unconditionally.
consequence: With no ingredients the player gets an empty mixer window instead of the classic 'You have no ingredients' refusal - cosmetic flow divergence only.

title: Dungeon fall damage never flashes the screen; the other three hosts do
claim: dungeonContext's own fall arm (reportActivity :2718-2723 - fed by both dungeon hosts, dungeon.js:418 and worldModes.js:2685) does hurtPlayer + FallDamage sound only; its 'ShowPlayerDamage screen flash pends the HUD arc (flagged)' comment is stale - flashPlayerDamage exists and this file calls it for arrows (:1701) and melee (:1945). DFU's ApplyPlayerFallDamage calls RemoveHealth (PlayerHealth.cs:49-58), whose first act is ShowPlayerDamage.Flash() (:36-38), so every damaging fall flashes. shared.applyFallLanding, the arm the other three hosts use (shared.js:531-547), calls flashPlayerDamage for this exact reason; the wave39 test pin covers shared.js and the enemy-blow sites but not this arm.
consequence: A damaging fall in any dungeon (standalone or world-hosted) deals HP with no red damage flash, while the identical fall outdoors or in a building flashes - a per-scene inconsistency DFU does not have.

title: Exterior Detect feeds pass no loot pool though dropped piles and corpses exist above ground
claim: world.js:1180-1183 and exterior.js:586-590 build createDetectFeed with entities only - no loot thunk - while dungeonContext.js:844-848 passes both pools. The HUD comments justify it as 'no loot PILES above ground (FLAGGED)' (world.js:3542-3545, exterior.js:1837-1839), but both hosts mount createDroppedLoot (player drops become world piles, world.js:819 / exterior.js:564) and both have lootable corpse containers (cityGuards/exteriorFoes lootTargets). DFU's PlayerGPS.UpdateNearbyObjects walks EVERY active DaggerfallLoot with no scene gate (PlayerGPS.cs:747, 766-776), so Detect Treasure outdoors marks dropped piles and corpses in DFU.
consequence: Detect Treasure cast outdoors shows no marker even standing over the player's own dropped pile or a guard/foe corpse; the same cast works in a dungeon. The flag's premise ('no loot above ground') has been false since droppedLoot was mounted in both hosts.

title: StockHouseContainer unported: private house containers are permanently empty
claim: DFU stocks a house container on first access (PlayerActivate.cs:911-913 -> StockHouseContainer): picks an item group from the privatePropertyItems tables by container model + building type, then mints items in a loop with a halving continue chance gated by DFRandom.rand()%100 > continueChance (DaggerfallLoot.cs:369-371) - DaggerfallLoot's only DFRandom draw. The port identifies house containers verbatim (systems/containers.js) but interiorContext.js:127-130 declares private furniture starts EMPTY, worldModes.js:2409-2417 transferAll()s the always-empty c.items, and no port code stocks them; the privatePropertyItems tables do not exist in src/.
consequence: Burgling or exploring any house in the port yields nothing from any container, ever; in DFU/classic the same containers produce the classic private-property loot (clothing, books, weapons, etc.) on first open.

title: Human-enemy gender roll substitutes Math.random for DFU's shared DFRandom draw
claim: DFU decides an unspecified-gender human enemy's gender with the shared LCG: GetTextureArchive does DFRandom.random_range(0,2)==0 -> Male else Female (DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:626), consuming one shared-stream draw per such enemy. The port rolls the same 50/50 with Math.random at the hosts (dungeonContext.js:924, also :531/:596 via MobileUnit ctor arg, exteriorFoes.js:86), consuming no shared draw.
consequence: One shared-stream draw per unspecified-gender human enemy is skipped vs DFU; DFU's draw rides the unseeded, frame-cadence-dependent stream position (nondeterministic between sessions) and the 50/50 distribution is identical, so no reproducible sequence breaks - negligible observable impact.

title: dungeonContext.destroy() skips the dead-mark on dropped piles; spawnCorpse lacks a context-alive guard
claim: droppedLoot's async mount guards only on pile.dead (droppedLoot.js:54) and every other removal site sets dead first (:93/:111/:129/:167 - protocol documented at :45-53). dungeonContext.destroy (:3066-3069) frees batches and clears _piles WITHOUT setting dead, so a pile dropped just before exiting whose texture is still warming mints a batch onto an orphan after destroy ran. Same class: spawnCorpse (:1449-1473) awaits getTexture and guards only '!f.dead' (:1459), so a foe killed right before exit mints a corpse batch into the destroyed context's lists.
consequence: One leaked GPU batch per exit-during-texture-warm (drop or first kill of an enemy type immediately before leaving). Rare, but violates the module's own documented ownership protocol.

title: tryEnter's failure path leaks the fully built interior context
claim: tryEnter builds the whole interior context (worldModes.js:2224 - GPU billboard batches plus voxelfolk race meshes) before computing the landing; a null landing throws 'no interior landing' (:2238) before interiorCtx is assigned, and both hosts only log it (world.js:3210, exterior.js:1538 catch -> console.error). Nothing calls ctx.destroy() on that path, so the build's GPU allocations are orphaned. In DFU a failed transition's objects still die with the Unity scene teardown; here the port owns every allocation and the error path drops them.
consequence: A building whose interior yields no enter markers and no doors leaks its full interior GPU allocation on every E-press (repeatable - the door is not marked bad). Reachable only on degenerate interior data I could not confirm exists in the shipped set.

title: audio.ensure guards its await with a boolean - second caller resolves before DAGGER.SND loads
claim: AudioEngine.ensure sets this._booted = true and returns before 'await this.init(fetchBytes)' completes (audio.js:69-88), so a concurrent second caller's await resolves while enabled is still false and its immediate playOneShot/play3d calls silently drop. The sibling MusicService documents and fixed this exact race ('AUDIT 19 F1/F11... The flag is now the PROMISE... A guard set before its own async work is not idempotence, it is a race with a flag on it', music.js:39-54); the sound engine kept the boolean shape.
consequence: One-shots requested between a first ensure starting and DAGGER.SND finishing are lost, not queued. Per-frame callers self-heal (torch loops retry on null handle), so impact today is marginal boot-window sound loss.

title: Exterior quicksave saves no live enemies (encounter foes + city guards)
claim: DFU's SaveData_v1 carries enemyData for every registered live enemy wherever the player stands (BuildSaveData :865, restored :1006), and SerializableStateManager.RestoreEnemyData (:404-425) re-instantiates each one from prefab on load (exterior handled by SerializableEnemy.cs:189-191). The port's worldQuickSave world half (world.js:1635-1641) carries only pixel/native coords/height/piles; exteriorFoes.foes and cityGuards.guards (live spell targets per world.js:1084) are saved nowhere, and worldQuickLoad restores only piles, then sets _lastEncMinutes to suppress spawn catch-up (world.js:1678).
consequence: Quicksave during a wilderness ambush or guard pursuit and quickload: every attacker despawns with no catch-up spawn - a free escape from any exterior fight that DFU's save round-trips intact.

title: Dungeon foe snapshot omits active effect bundles (instancedEffectBundles)
claim: SerializableEnemy saves each enemy's instancedEffectBundles (:120) and restores them via RestoreInstancedBundleSaveData (:222). The port's foes ARE effect targets - applySpellToFoe (hostMagic.js:106-107) runs applySpell on foe.entity and effects.js pushes onto target.activeEffects (:519-547) - but collectWorld's per-foe record (dungeonContext.js:1745-1756) carries only health/dead/feet/yaw/items/hostile/encountered/magicka; f.entity.activeEffects is never snapshotted and applyWorld (:1768-1781) never restores it.
consequence: Paralysis, continuous damage, soul trap marks, and every other timed effect on every dungeon enemy silently ends on quicksave+quickload: a paralyzed boss wakes, a burning foe stops burning - in DFU the bundles survive the load.

title: daedraSummonDay/daedraSummonIndex mutated on the entity but never saved or restored
claim: DFU persists PlayerEntity.DaedraSummonDay and DaedraSummonIndex one-for-one (GetSaveData :164-165, RestoreSaveData :332-333). The port stores the coven's remembered daily roll on the same entity - daedraForSummoner mutates state.daedraSummonIndex/state.daedraSummonDay (daedraSummoning.js:109-111) and worldModes.js:1635 passes state: playerEntity - but ENTITY_FIELDS (save.js:30-58) omits both, so snapshotPlayer never writes them and restorePlayer neither restores nor clears them.
consequence: The witch coven's daedra-of-the-day re-derives instead of restoring: reload from a fresh boot and the coven re-rolls (save-scum until the prince you want answers); an in-session backward load keeps the post-save roll instead of the saved one. DFU round-trips the roll exactly.

title: Foe maxHealth (startingHealth) and fatigue not round-tripped
claim: SerializableEnemy saves startingHealth (entity.MaxHealth, :109) and currentFatigue (:111) and restores both (:175 MaxHealth, :177 SetFatigue). The port's collectWorld saves only health/magicka; makeEnemyEntity re-rolls maxHealth with Math.random on every rebuild (characters/enemyEntity.js:80 rollEnemyClassMaxHealth, :85 Range(min,max+1)), and foe fatigue is live drained/restored state (dungeonContext.js:1109-1110 foe sinks) that applyWorld never touches.
consequence: On a rebuild-then-restore load (standalone ?dungeon ?load path) each monster's max HP re-rolls, so restored health can exceed the new max and enemy toughness shifts across a load; on any in-session quickload a fatigue-drained foe keeps its live value instead of the saved one.

title: Interior host cannot save at all (savingPrevented hardwired true)
claim: DFU saves inside buildings: SerializablePlayer stores exteriorDoors + buildingDiscoveryData when IsPlayerInsideBuilding (:183-187) and SaveLoadManager.cs:1410-1418 restores the interior context on load. The port's interior mode wires the pause window with savingPrevented: () => true (worldModes.js:3560; 'You cannot save now.' per pauseWindow.js:192-195) and mounts no quickSave/quickLoad in its routeKey ctx, so F9 inside a building is a silent no-op. Flagged in-code as unbuilt (worldModes.js:3416-3419) - reported so the audit ledger carries the row; refuters should not treat it as an unknown regression.
consequence: A player inside any shop, tavern, temple, or house cannot save the game; DFU saves anywhere. Progress since the last exterior/dungeon save is lost on a crash inside.

title: Weapon drawn/sheathed state not in the envelope
claim: DFU saves data.weaponDrawn (:175) and restores weaponManager.Sheathed = !data.weaponDrawn (:420). The port's sheath state lives on weaponRig.playerWeapon.sheathed in both saving hosts (world.js:892, dungeonContext.js:1482) but snapshotPlayer carries no field for it and neither host's quickLoad touches the rig.
consequence: A save made with the weapon drawn always loads with it in the rig's default state - the player must re-draw after every load; DFU restores the drawn state.

title: Player yaw, pitch, and crouch state not saved with position
claim: PlayerPositionData_v1 carries yaw, pitch, and isCrouching (:212-214), restored by RestorePosition. The port saves only lastPlayerFeet (dungeonContext.js:2729) and restores via setPlayerPos(extras.position) (:2767) - a bare 3-vector; the world host's envelope (world.js:1636) likewise carries coordinates only. The port has crouch (player/motor.js P12) and mouselook yaw/pitch, so the state exists to lose.
consequence: Every load resets facing to the motor default and stands the player up; a save made crouched in a 0.9-height crawlspace loads standing at that spot.

title: Static NPC generated names use the race's name bank; DFU always uses the region's
claim: staticNpcName defaults bank = bankForRace(data.race) (staticNpc.js:211). DFU: SetRuntimeData sets npcData.nameBank = GetNameBankOfCurrentRegion() (StaticNPC.cs:309, always Breton/Redguard) and GetDisplayName calls FullName(npcData.nameBank, gender) (:325-326); TalkManager.cs:2848 uses the region bank too; nothing assigns a race bank. Both production callers omit nameBank (worldModes.js:976, 1364). The port knows the law for mobiles (world.js:506, exterior.js:1367 pass getNameBankOfRegion citing MobilePersonNPC.cs:214) and staticNpc.js:233 re-exports getNameBankOfRegion, but no static caller uses it. Factions without a race: line parse race 0 = Nord on both sides.
consequence: Any interior static NPC whose derived race differs from the region race (incl. the Nord default on race-less factions) is named from the wrong bank - Nord '...sen' surnames in Breton/Redguard towns where DFU generates regional names.

verify.reason: DFU StaticNPC.cs:309 always sets npcData.nameBank = GetNameBankOfCurrentRegion() before GetDisplayName (:325-326) uses it - region-based, never race-based. Port's staticNpcName (staticNpc.js:206,211) defaults to bankForRace(data.race); its only two callers (worldModes.js:976,1364) never pass nameBank. Port already has getNameBankOfRegion wired for mobile NPCs (world.js:506) but never for static NPCs - an unported gap, not a departure.

title: IsChildNPCData is unported; isChildNPC is read in three places and written nowhere
claim: DFU StaticNPC.IsChildNPCData (:342-350) flags children by IsChildNPCTexture(archive, record) or factionID == 514, gating quest offers (TalkManager.cs:755-770) and the work pool (:2842). The port has no equivalent: grep of src/ shows isChildNPC/isChild only read (worldModes.js:979,1366 pass !!pn.isChildNPC; npcSession.js:466,653) and never written, and staticNpc.js carries neither the 514 constant nor the child texture table. The flag is constant false.
consequence: A child NPC in a castle can pass the isCastleNpcOfferingQuest door and offer quests where DFU excludes children from both questor arms; the work-pool child exclusion is inert.

verify.reason: DFU gates both questor arms on IsChildNPC (TalkManager.cs:755,769 -> StaticNPC.cs:342-350: texture table or factionID==514). Port reads isChildNPC/isChild at worldModes.js:979,1366 and npcSession.js:466,653 but writes it nowhere - pn never carries it, staticNpc.js has neither the 514 constant nor a child-texture table, so it's always false and the !isChildNPC guards (npcSession.js:468,472) never exclude a child. audit24_onehome.test.js:225 pins the always-false `!!pn.isChildNPC` shape verbatim.

title: Bow shots always use RangedAttack1 records; HasRangedAttack2 mobiles should use records 25-29
claim: DFU picks the bow state: RangedAttack1 only if (HasRangedAttack1 && !HasRangedAttack2), else RangedAttack2 (EnemyMotor.cs:594-597); GetStateAnims maps RangedAttack2 to RangedAttack2Anims records 25-29 (DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:840-841; EnemyBasics.cs:103-113). The port has a single 'ranged' state always returning RANGED_ATTACK1_ANIMS records 20-24 (mobileUnit.js:120), and hosts key one rangedStriking flag. Rows 130 (Battlemage) and 133 (Nightblade) carry hasRangedAttack2:true plus castsMagic (enemyBasics.js:2103, :2293), so hasBowAttack is true and their bow shots draw records 20-24 - which for these hasSpellAnimation rows are the SPELL-casting records.
consequence: A Battlemage or Nightblade shooting its bow renders its spell-casting sprite animation instead of its bow animation (archive 489/490 records 20-24 vs 25-29); the arrow still fires on the -1 marker.

verify.reason: C#: EnemyMotor.cs:594-597 picks RangedAttack2 when HasRangedAttack2; DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:840-841 maps it to EnemyBasics.RangedAttack2Anims (records 25-29, EnemyBasics.cs:103-109), distinct from RangedAttack1Anims (20-24). JS: mobileUnit.js:120 always returns RANGED_ATTACK1_ANIMS for state 'ranged'; no RANGED_ATTACK2_ANIMS exists in src/. enemyBasics.js rows '130'/'133' (Battlemage/Nightblade, lines 2094-2103/2288-2293) have hasRangedAttack2+hasSpellAnimation=true, so bow shot renders same records as spell cast. No pin covers this.

title: Bow-band shots and spell casts not suppressed during knockback (CanAct chain incomplete)
claim: DFU KnockbackMovement sets CanAct=false while KnockbackSpeed>0 (EnemyMotor.cs:317) and TakeAction runs only under `if (CanAct)` (:171-172), so DoRangedAttack (:469 - the 1/32 bow and 1/40 spell rolls) and DoTouchSpell (:473) never run mid-knockback; the Hurt state also counts as IsPlayingOneShot (Base/MobileUnit.cs:153-168), blocking the rolls at :587. The port models only the giveUpTimer part of CanAct: the band arm (enemyAttack.js:127-134) and both EnemyCaster branches (enemyCasting.js:110-130) keep running while ai.knockbackSpeed>0; hosts gate only paralysis/hostility (dungeonContext.js:2290/2312, exteriorFoes.js:294/299). Melee correctly keeps running (CanAct-independent in DFU).
consequence: For the ~0.2-0.5s knockback window after each solid player hit, a port archer can loose its 1/32 bow shot and a caster can cast touch/ranged spells; DFU enemies cannot act at all during knockback - ranged foes fight back through hit-stun.

verify.reason: C#: KnockbackMovement sets CanAct=false whenever KnockbackSpeed>0 (EnemyMotor.cs:272-317); TakeAction (incl. DoRangedAttack:469/DoTouchSpell:473) runs only `if(CanAct)` (:171-172). JS: enemyAttack.js:127-136 rolls bow shot with no knockbackSpeed check; enemyCasting.js update (103-132) likewise none. Hosts dungeonContext.js:2290/2312 and exteriorFoes.js:294/299 gate calls only on paralysis/hostility, never knockbackSpeed. No contradicting pin (checked audit24_characters/wave32/wave33, which only pin the paralysis half).

title: Detour override reordered ahead of DoRangedAttack in the decision chain
claim: DFU TakeAction calls DoRangedAttack at :469 and DoTouchSpell at :473 BEFORE the `if (avoidObstaclesTimer > 0) AttemptMove(...)` detour arm at :481-484, so an in-band shooter with sight+detection stands off and shoots even while a detour timer runs (the timer just decays). The port's _classicTick takes the detour arm first (enemyMotor.js:943-951) and only then calls _doRangedAttack (:956); its comment miscites :480-484 as "TakeAction's FIRST branch". test/audit24_wave35.test.js:113-114 pins this ordering ("the detour override first of all") - the pin restates the port, not the C#, which puts the detour after both attack calls.
consequence: For up to 0.75s after an obstacle/fall probe fires, an archer or ranged caster inside the 6-51.2 band with the target in sight keeps walking its detour instead of standing off as DFU does; shots still roll from the attack component, so it shoots on the move.

verify.reason: C#: TakeAction calls DoRangedAttack(:469)/DoTouchSpell(:473), both return-early on success, BEFORE the detour arm at :481-484. JS: `_classicTick` checks `if(detouring)` first (enemyMotor.js:943, returns 944-951) then `_doRangedAttack` (:956) - reversed order; the port's own comment (940-941) misdescribes this as DFU's 'FIRST branch'. test/audit24_wave35.test.js:113-114 only string-matches the port's own source order ('detour override first of all'), never checking real C# line order - so it's confirming evidence, not a refutation.

title: searchMult not reset when GiveUpTimer expires (or while pacified)
claim: DFU HandleNoAction resets searchMult=0 on ANY of its three arms - target null, GiveUpTimer <= 0, or PredictedTargetPos sentinel (EnemyMotor.cs:357-366, searchMult=0 at :362) - every FixedUpdate. The port resets it only on the predictedTargetPos===null arm (enemyMotor.js:935); the gave-up arm at :931 (`!detected && giveUpTimer <= 0`) returns without touching searchMult, and a pacified foe skips _classicTick entirely (:1039) so no arm runs. The stale ramp is only cleared later by _getDestination's clear-path arm (:869).
consequence: A foe that ramped its search (searchMult up to 10) then gave up resumes a later non-clear-path pursuit aiming up to 10 units past the last-known position instead of at it, walking somewhere DFU's freshly-reset foe would not.

verify.reason: C#: HandleNoAction (EnemyMotor.cs:357-366) resets searchMult=0 on all 3 arms (target null, GiveUpTimer<=0, sentinel), every FixedUpdate. JS: enemyMotor.js:931 (gave-up arm) does not reset searchMult; only line 935 (sentinel arm) and line 869 (clear-path in _getDestination) do. `_classicTick` (holding both arms) only runs `if(!paralyzed&&!knocked&&isHostile)` (line 1039), so a pacified/knocked foe skips both. Stale searchMult is consumed as an offset in the search branch (878-884), matching the claimed consequence.

title: Touch casts gated on the attack machine being Idle; DFU DoTouchSpell has no one-shot gate
claim: DFU's DoTouchSpell condition (EnemyMotor.cs:621-623) has no isPlayingOneShot term; the only one-shot early-out above it in TakeAction is OneShotPauseActionsWhilePlaying (:465), true only for SeducerTransform states (Base/MobileUnit.cs:174-184). So a DFU foe whose melee timer is 0 mid-swing casts the touch spell, ChangeEnemyState(Spell) cutting the swing. The port adds `idle` (attack.machine.state === 'Idle') to the touch arm (enemyCasting.js:107, :110), skipping the cast until the swing ends. Reachable when ResetMeleeTimer floors to 0: 1500 - 50*(level-10) + 450*(reflexes-2) <= 0, i.e. player level ~22+ at low reflexes, ~40 at average.
consequence: Against high-level players, a touch-caster in melee range delays its cast by up to a full swing (~0.5-1s) and its interrupted melee blow lands where DFU would have cancelled it into the spell.

verify.reason: C#: DoTouchSpell (EnemyMotor.cs:621-623) has no one-shot term; TakeAction's only one-shot gate (:465, OneShotPauseActionsWhilePlaying) is SeducerTransform-only (MobileUnit.cs:174-183); ChangeEnemyState (MobileUnit.cs:137-147) switches unconditionally, interrupting a swing. ResetMeleeTimer (EnemyAttack.cs:114-131) floors to 0 at level ~22+(low reflexes)/~40(avg), matching claim's math. JS: enemyCasting.js:107,110 adds `idle=attack.machine.state==='Idle'` as an extra required term DFU lacks. No contradicting pin found.

title: GiveUpTimer frozen during paralysis/knockback; DFU UpdateTimers runs before the CanAct gate

title: envAttack skips Receive(Attack) on doors; DFU fires the door's action record before bashing

title: Port persists activationCount across save/load; DFU resets it to 0
claim: SerializableActionObject (:55-88) persists only position/rotation/currentState/tween percentage; SerializableActionDoor (:67-101) adds lock and FailedSkillLevel. consequence: After loading, DFU re-shows a DoorText door's text and holds it shut on first click, and restarts Hurt21's every-20th phase; the port does neither, so trap cadence and first-click door behavior diverge after any save/load.

title: Nature scatter rect exclusion gated on pre-expansion mins; DFU re-checks the expanded rect per tile
claim: DFU LayoutNature expands the location rect by natureClearance=4 only when the un-expanded rect has x>0 && y>0 (TerrainNature.cs:60-66), then in the tile loop re-evaluates `rect.x > 0 && rect.y > 0 && rect.Contains(tilePos)` on the EXPANDED rect (TerrainNature.cs:124) - so when expansion pushes xMin or yMin to <= 0, DFU disables the containment test entirely and scatters nature inside the location footprint. The port (terrainNature.js:72-79) builds the rect when the PRE-expansion mins are > 0 and then applies containment unconditionally at line 112, never re-checking the expanded mins.
consequence: For a location whose pre-clearance rect min on either axis lies in (0, 4] (only possible for 8-block-wide/tall locations, since the tile origin is 0 only then), DFU places nature billboards over the town footprint while the port suppresses them - a visible foliage difference at large walled cities with narrow edge blend space.

verify.reason: TerrainNature.cs:60-66: rect.xMin/xMax +-= clearance mutates the underlying x/y fields (Unity Rect semantics); the tile-loop reject at :124 re-tests rect.x>0&&rect.y>0 against the EXPANDED value, so a pre-expansion min in (0,4] disables containment. Port (terrainNature.js:72-79) gates rect-building on PRE-expansion mins only, then at :112 tests mere truthiness of rect with no re-check - always excludes where DFU sometimes wouldn't.

title: Dungeon water footstep hysteresis dropped: single 0.57 threshold vs DFU 0.57-enter/0.95-exit

title: Book layout merges Text tokens into one row and centers the justify-terminated line, unlike CreateBookLabels
claim: DFU CreateBookLabels creates a SEPARATE label per Text token (:254), each its own row via LayoutBookLabels (y += label.Size.y, :326), with alignment applied only to labels created AFTER a justify token (:241-245). The port (bookReader.js:97-110) concatenates a line's Text tokens into ONE row and applies JustifyCenter retroactively (current.center=true, :103). For Text('A'),0xFD,Text('B'),NewLine (the shape the port's test PAGE1 models), DFU renders 'A' Left and 'B' Center on two rows; the port renders one centered row 'AB'. test/books.test.js:140-153 pins the port (['CenteredOffset line', true]) while citing the C# - the pin restates the port.
consequence: Classic books using 0xFD line terminators (centered title pages, poems) render consecutive centered lines run together on one over-wide row, with centering shifted one line versus DFU.

title: shouldClose drops the unconditional Escape close, making quest and infection videos unskippable
claim: DFU closes the vid window on 'endOnAnyKey && AnyKeyDown || GetBackButtonDown() || EndOfFile && Playing' (:140-142); GetBackButtonDown is Escape keydown (InputManager.cs:1065-1067), checked OUTSIDE the endOnAnyKey gate, so EndOnAnyKey=false videos (PlayVideo.cs:78, VampirismInfection.cs:126/136, LycanthropyInfection.cs:114) still skip on Escape. The port's shouldClose (videoPlayer.js:234-236) is '(endOnAnyKey && anyKeyDown) || (endOfFile && playing)' with no back-button arm, and shared.js:936 passes endOnAnyKey:false for infection videos - its comment even asserts they 'cannot be skipped', misreading DFU.
consequence: The vampirism/lycanthropy dream and turning videos and quest PlayVideo actions cannot be skipped with Escape in the port; in DFU Escape always closes the video window.
